intel.t: A populist cost of living pitch: she will take on corporations and billionaires, will not be bought, and Masterson is Brownback 2.0 who failed to deliver property tax relief with a supermajority.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: Masterson and Trump call her a socialist and the most radical candidate in state history, and the RGA says she opposed capping property taxes and flipped on data centers after voting for SB 98.
Organized labor, with the Teamsters, the Kansas AFL-CIO, KNEA, AFT, SEIU, UAW and UFCW, plus a reunited party establishment led by Kelly.

Name recognition: 12 percent had not heard of her and 15 percent were neutral in Emerson's September 15 to 16 poll, which had her down 44 to 51. Unaffiliated voters outnumber Democrats by more than 50,000.

On October 26 she called Masterson a stooge for Big Tech after Building the Future put more than $1.5 million behind him; a week earlier she thanked Trump for shouting her out after he called her a radical lunatic.
She had $64,933.65 cash on July 23 against Masterson's $430,211.71, and the RGA's about $6.9 million reservation dwarfs KVI's $2.755 million.

bottom: Holscher won the Democratic primary on August 4, 2026 with 48.6 percent over Ethan Corson, the candidate Gov. Laura Kelly had endorsed, per the Kansas Reflector on October 20, 2026, https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/trump-affirms-endorsement-ty-masterson-kansas-governors-race-belittles-cindy-holscher. She faces Senate President Ty Masterson for the open seat. Kelly is term limited.

Her own money is thin. Her July report shows $412,630.21 raised from January 1 to July 23, 2026, $527,588.29 spent, and $64,933.65 left, per the filing posted by the Sunflower State Journal, https://sunflowerstatejournal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Campaign-Finance-Receipts-and-Expenditures-Report-129.pdf. Masterson ended the same period with $430,211.71.
Three interests combine money and a decision:

**Organized labor.** The Teamsters conference, the Kansas AFL-CIO, KNEA, AFT, SEIU Local 513, UAW Local 31, UFCW Local 2 and AFGE back her. The lever is school funding, Medicaid expansion and union labor on data center builds.

intel.t: Property tax relief and affordability: no Kansan taxed out of a home, farm or business, a 3 percent cap on assessed value growth, and Holscher as too radical for Kansas.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: Brownback 2.0 plus a Koch funded GoCreate post paying $217,350 that rivals call a no-show job, along with big tech tax breaks and his 2010 bankruptcy; he denies writing the Brownback plan and WSU defends his role.
Trump's base plus farm groups, with the Farm Bureau PAC, Kansas Grain and Feed and Agribusiness Retailers, and some building trades and transport unions.
He is underwater at 40 favorable and 44 unfavorable while Holscher is net positive, and he led independents only 47 to 45 in Emerson's September 15 to 16 poll.
Building the Future, a pro data center super PAC, put more than $1.5 million behind him on October 26, a week after Trump reaffirmed his endorsement at a Park City rally.
He held $430,211.71 on July 23 to Holscher's $64,933.65, and the RGA reserved about $6.9 million to the DGA's $2.755 million through KVI.

bottom: Masterson won a seven candidate Republican primary on August 4, 2026 with 43 percent, carried by President Trump's endorsement, per the Kansas Reflector on October 20, 2026, https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/trump-affirms-endorsement-ty-masterson-kansas-governors-race-belittles-cindy-holscher. Trump reaffirmed it at a Park City rally on October 19.

His July report shows $766,535.24 raised from January 1 to July 23, 2026, $1,023,845.63 spent, and $430,211.71 left, per his filing, https://www.kansas.gov/ethics/CFAScanned/StWide/2026ElecCycle/202607/SW01TM_202607.pdf. That is about $365,000 more cash than Holscher held on the same date.
Three interests combine money and a decision:
**The RGA.** Right Direction PAC reserved about $6.9 million against Holscher.

D.t: Cindy Holscher leads by 0.4 in the forecast and wins 52% of simulations. The cushion is about 4,945 votes; a one point swing is about 5,750 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +8.0 and D +8.6. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +2.9. Your best recent poll is Washington Post/Schar School at D +6.0; your worst is On Point Polling at R +6.5. 10 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Johnson, a projected net 81,722 votes; Douglas, a projected net 31,241 votes; Wyandotte, a projected net 23,728 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sedgwick, D +4.2, 16.1% of the vote; Leavenworth, R +6.5, 2.7% of the vote; Crawford, R +5.4, 1.2% of the vote; Harvey, R +6.2, 1.2% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Cindy Holscher runs furthest behind in McPherson, Butler, Miami. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 88% of voters, 46 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.39 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 70% of voters, 48 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.50 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.95 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Cindy Holscher: Immigration voters 18 to 81, Small counties 30 to 67, Incomes $125K and up 39 to 59. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$65K cash against $430K. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 45% of the 282,232 ballots in Kansas so far, against 41% for the other party. That is 11.3 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
